shotCaption: makitatools.com on a 390-pixel phone screen, as captured for this review

findings.title: The first screen on a phone is two overlays and no content
findings.found: Rendered at phone width, the promotional popup runs off the right edge of the screen and the cookie notice covers the bottom. A visitor sees neither the hero nor a product until both are dismissed, and the clipped popup cannot be read in full.
findings.why: A large share of visits to a manufacturer site now come from a phone, often from a job site or a dealer counter. A clipped first screen reads as broken, and most visitors leave before they see a product.
findings.fix: Make the promo modal responsive or suppress it below tablet width, and let the cookie bar collapse to a single line. Front-end work measured in hours, not a redesign.

findings.title: Your email domain can be impersonated
findings.found: makitatools.com publishes no SPF record and no DMARC record, while running its own mail servers (mx1 and mx2.makitatools.com). Public DNS, checked September 2026.
findings.why: Anyone can send email that appears to come from an @makitatools.com address, and receiving servers have no published policy telling them to reject it. Dealer invoice fraud and phishing aimed at your own staff are the usual outcomes.
findings.fix: Publish SPF, sign mail with DKIM, and add a DMARC policy. These are DNS changes, not a project: start at p=none to monitor, then move to quarantine and reject.

findings.title: A heavy homepage with nothing deferred
findings.found: The homepage HTML alone is 304 KB, and it loads 122 images up front with none marked for lazy loading.
findings.why: On mobile data the whole page downloads before it is usable. Every extra second of load time costs visitors, and image weight is the most common cause.
findings.fix: Lazy-load images below the fold and trim the page. Standard optimizations on the existing site, with no design change.

findings.title: Six main headings on one page
findings.found: The homepage carries six H1 headings.
findings.why: Search engines read the main heading to understand what a page is about. Six of them dilute that signal and usually mean the page template has drifted.
findings.fix: One H1 per page, with product sections as H2s. A template fix.

findings.title: A security policy that is not enforcing anything
findings.found: The site sends a Content-Security-Policy header, but it allows scripts and images from any origin, so it blocks nothing.
findings.why: That header is what stops injected scripts, such as card skimmers and ad injection, from running on your pages. A wildcard policy gives the appearance of protection without the effect.
findings.fix: Tighten the policy to the domains the site actually uses, rolled out in report-only mode first so nothing breaks.
